---
title: "Modules"
---

Imagine this site as a short trip with four stops.

You begin in a garden and a kitchen—plants, processing, and a mug. You travel inward into the body and brain. You climb out again into history, monasteries, warm hands, and ritual. You end in a lab where people play careful games about risk and trust. Each stop answers a question the previous stop left hanging.

Nothing here requires a science degree. Each chapter opens with a hook, walks you through the facts in story order, and leaves a door open to the next chapter.

## The itinerary

| Stop | The question that pulls you forward | Open |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. The Chemical Core | Why do two cups from the same plant taste—and feel—so different? | [Chapter 1](module-01.qmd) |
| 2. Body, Brain & Mood | Why does tea so often feel awake *and* calmer than coffee? | [Chapter 2](module-02.qmd) |
| 3. History, Ritual & Warmth | Is tea only chemistry—or also empire, ritual, and a warm hand? | [Chapter 3](module-03.qmd) |
| 4. Decisions & Choices | Does the cup change how we choose—and how do researchers even measure that? | [Chapter 4](module-04.qmd) |

## Four branches inside each chapter

The owner’s source packs use the same four-branch pattern in every module. The site keeps that skeleton so you can bounce between story and pack without getting lost.

| Chapter | The four branches (story beats) |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Chemical Core | Two plants · Green vs black processing · Brewing · Three compounds |
| 2. Body & mind | How drinks act in the brain · Brain-wave patterns · Stress hormones · Body signals |
| 3. Socio-ritual | Trade history · Monastic history · Warmth and trust · Ritual and stress |
| 4. Decision | Dual-process thinking · Risk and waiting · Games of trust · Study protocols |

## If you only have ten minutes

**“What’s in my cup?”**  
Start with [Cup reference](../cup-reference.qmd), then Chapter 1’s brewing and compounds sections.

**“Why awake but not jittery?”**  
Go straight to [Chapter 2](module-02.qmd), then the linkages note on L-theanine timing and calm brain waves.

**“Is tea only chemistry?”**  
No. [Chapter 3](module-03.qmd) is the zoom-out: trade, monasteries, warm mugs, brewing breaks.

**“Do drinks change choices?”**  
[Chapter 4](module-04.qmd)—with the packs’ caveats that lab doses are not your everyday mug.

When you are ready to begin at the beginning, open [Chapter 1](module-01.qmd). The water is already hot.
